To eschew something means to deliberately and consciously choose to avoid it — typically as a matter of personal principle, discipline, or strong preference.

The single most important thing to understand about "eschew" is that it is never accidental. When you eschew something, you are making an active, intentional decision to stay away from it. This is what separates it from the simpler word "avoid," which can describe both accidental and deliberate distance.

Think of it this way:

  • If you accidentally skip a meeting, you "avoided" it.
  • But if you have made a personal rule to never attend unnecessary meetings, you "eschew" them.

The act of eschewing something is always a choice — usually a firm, consistent, and often principle-driven one.
What Kinds of Things Can You Eschew?

You can eschew practically anything you consciously choose to stay away from:

  • Behaviors: violence, gossip, shortcuts, confrontation
  • Foods or substances: alcohol, meat, processed food, sugar
  • Approaches or styles: complexity, flashiness, sentimentality
  • Practices or conventions: social media, small talk, formal attire

"Eschew" carries a slightly moral or principled flavor. When you say someone eschews something, it often implies a thoughtful, sustained commitment, not just a casual preference. Compare:

  • "He avoids fast food." — He just stays away from it.
  • "He eschews fast food." — It sounds like a deliberate lifestyle principle he holds.

This is why "eschew" often appears in formal or serious writing — essays, journalism, literature, speeches — rather than in everyday casual conversation. Saying "I eschew drama" in a text message would sound a little stiff. In writing or formal speech, however, it is elegant and precise.

These examples will show you exactly how it works in context:

  1. "She has always eschewed violence as a means of solving problems."

She has made a conscious, principled choice to never use violence — not just once, but as a consistent rule.

  1. "The chef eschews processed ingredients, insisting on only fresh, local produce."

He deliberately avoids processed ingredients as part of his cooking philosophy.

  1. "As a minimalist, he eschews unnecessary possessions."

He intentionally keeps away from owning things he doesn't need.

  1. "The author eschews complicated language, preferring to write in simple, direct sentences."

She makes a deliberate stylistic choice to avoid complexity.

Notice the pattern: in every case, the avoidance is intentional, consistent, and rooted in some kind of personal stance or value.

"Eschew" is a transitive verb, meaning it always needs an object — there must be something being avoided:

  • ✅ "She eschews drama." (correct — has an object)
  • ❌ "She eschews." (incorrect — missing an object)

You can also follow it with a gerund (an -ing word used as a noun):

  • ✅ "He eschews eating junk food."

It also works in the past tense and continuous forms:

  • "She eschewed the spotlight throughout her career."
  • "He has always been eschewing shortcuts."
How It Compares to Similar Words

Understanding where "eschew" sits among its neighbors will sharpen your grasp of it:

Avoid — more neutral and broad; can be accidental or intentional. "Eschew" is always intentional.

Shun — similar strength, but typically used for avoiding people or groups, sometimes with a sense of social rejection or disgust. "Eschew" is more commonly used for behaviors, habits, or practices.

Abstain from — usually refers to physically refraining from a specific urge or act, like abstaining from alcohol or voting. "Eschew" is broader and more principle-oriented.

Forgo — means to go without something, often a pleasure or benefit, implying a degree of sacrifice. "Eschew" doesn't carry that sense of sacrifice as strongly.

Renounce — stronger and more dramatic; often implies a formal or public declaration of giving something up. "Eschew" is quieter and more personal.

So "eschew" is more deliberate than "avoid," more broadly applicable than "abstain from," less socially charged than "shun," and less dramatic than "renounce." It is the go-to word when you want to convey a quiet but firm, principle-based avoidance.
The antonyms of "eschew" include: embrace, adopt, pursue, indulge in. These are all actions of going toward something, whereas "eschew" is always about moving away from it.
One-Line Summary to Remember It By
To eschew something = to make a deliberate, principled, ongoing choice to stay away from it.
